sources.title: Consultation: Openreach's proposed commercial offers
sources.evidence_location: official HTML status, provisional-view and closing-date sections
sources.geography: United Kingdom wholesale fixed telecoms markets
facts: The consultation was published on 28 July 2026
It closes at 5pm on 27 August 2026
Ofcom provisionally proposes withdrawal of one Incremental New to Openreach Customer Offer
Ofcom does not provisionally propose intervention for the other notified offers
limitations: Wholesale pricing review is not premises coverage evidence

sources.title: Call for Inputs: Openreach’s proposed commercial offers
sources.evidence_location: official HTML notification, scope and closing-date sections
sources.geography: United Kingdom wholesale fixed telecoms markets
facts: Openreach notified several pricing offers on 1 June 2026
Ofcom published the call for inputs on 2 June 2026
Responses closed at 5pm on 19 June 2026
The page distinguishes conditional and geographic offers
limitations: A call for inputs is not a final regulatory decision
Pricing offers do not establish address-level broadband availability

sources.title: Statement: Promoting competition and investment in fibre networks - Telecoms Access Review 2026-31
sources.evidence_location: official HTML statement summary and update-documents section
facts: The statement was published on 17 March 2026
It regulates relevant fixed telecoms markets from April 2026 to March 2031
The decisions are intended to promote competition and investment in gigabit-capable networks
The page records a May 2026 modification update
limitations: Market regulation is not local coverage evidence
The HTML summary does not replace detailed conditions in the documents

sources.title: Telecoms Access Review 2026
facts: The hub records the March 2026 final TAR statement
It records a May 2026 modification of SMP conditions
It records a June 2026 call for inputs on Openreach offers
It separates statements, consultations and updates by date
limitations: A programme hub is lineage evidence, not parcel evidence
Open and closed processes must remain distinct

sources.title: Statement: Proposal to apply code powers to London Fibre Group Limited
sources.evidence_kind: Electronic Communications Code final direction process
sources.evidence_location: official HTML status, dates and Code-powers description
facts: The consultation was published on 11 March 2026
The final statement was published on 15 May 2026
The page concerns London Fibre Group Limited
Code powers can assist construction and maintenance of communications infrastructure
limitations: Code powers are an operator authorisation, not network deployment
The direction does not prove service at a premises
